messages:
incident-bot: Pager: production -> inference-prod-canary: sustained 5xx spike (18% over 5m). Error signature: model-server init/container crashloop. Severity: P1. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1755554321
deploy-bot: Deploy event: 2026-03-17T12:01Z commit abc123 - feature gate 'enable_dynamic_schema' toggled to canary (10%)
alice: I'm taking the pager, on it.
bob: @alice oncall here — what's the initial hypothesis?
carol: That feature flips a tiny DB migration which adds vector_meta to embeddings. We dark-launched earlier but this flip applied migration in init container for canary.
frank: Logs from inf-canary pod (svc=inf-canary):
```
[12:03:14] migration:init ERROR DBError: column "vector_meta" does not exist
[12:03:14] runtime FATAL unhandled exception -> exit(1)
[12:03:14] kube: restarting container
```
alice: So init-migration failing -> pod crashloop. HPA then scaled up more replicas and made more init jobs race?
carol: Exactly. HPA surge triggered multiple init containers concurrently; migration isn't leader-guarded so some pods see partial state and crash on queries.
dave: Any customer impact yet?
emily: Support sees increased 502s and 3 paying customers opened tickets ~12:04-12:06. Tentative impact to a small percentage of requests routed to canary.
bob: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) toggle feature off for canary (emergency), 2) scale HPA down to 1, 3) rollback canary deployment to previous stable revision, 4) cordon any nodes showing oom or eviction storms.
alice: Executing step 1: turning feature.enable_dynamic_schema -> OFF for canary cohort via admin console... done. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Feature flag change applied to canary cohort at 12:05Z.
bob: Scaling HPA: `kubectl scale hpa inf-canary --replicas=1 -n prod` -> executed.
frank: Deleting failing pods to force fresh start: `kubectl delete pod -l app=inf-canary -n prod` -> done, new pods pending.
carol: Rolling back to revision 42: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inf-canary -n prod --to-revision=42` — starting now.
alice: Monitoring metrics and pod readiness.
deploy-bot: Rollout undo submitted, new replica set = rs-42 coming up.
frank: New pods started, logs look clean. Errors dropped to ~1.2% in the last 5m window.
emily: Drafted customer message: "We experienced elevated errors due to a canary migration; rollback in progress; service degradation affecting a subset of requests. We'll send a follow-up once stabilized."
dave: Good. Post-incident actions we should track?
carol: Short list: 1) Make migrations leader-elected / serial (no concurrent init migrations), 2) Add migration readiness & timeout so failed init doesn't keep crashing service, 3) Prevent init migrations from running when HPA > 1 (or use a separate job), 4) Add feature-gate rollback runbook and automated revert for failing canaries.
alice: Also cordoned node gpu-07 (oom events) and drained noisy pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — cordon done.
grace: I'll open an incident ticket and own the follow-up. Scheduling postmortem with owners: @carol, @frank, @alice, DB owner. Downgrading severity P1 -> P2 after rollback and stabilization.
bob: Confirmed last checks: error rate stable, HPA kept at 1 until we add migration gating.
emily: Support will update customers in 30m with final status.
dave: Thanks everyone. Add retro items to next infra planning.
alice: Closing pager for now; keeping watch for 1h. :eyes: :thumbsup:
grace: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1755554321. Postmortem owner assigned.
frank: Quick note: snippet of the failing init job config we need to change:
```
initContainers:
  - name: run-migration
    image: migrations:stable
    command: ["/bin/migrate", "--apply"]
    # currently runs on every pod start -> needs leader lock
```
carol: Agreed, we'll convert to a Job with leader lock or use DB advisory locks.
bob: Any blockers for rollback validation?
alice: None. All checked.
incident-bot: Incident auto-update: P2, rollback successful, monitoring for regression.
